An elbow-length-sleeved crew-neck cotton T-shirt, a real plain T-shirt and not a real garment, covered edge to edge in an all-over sublimation print that covers the entire shirt, designed to make the shirt look like the outfit of a teacher. The print covers every part of the shirt from the ribbed collar band to the hem and out to both sleeve hems, and wraps around the side seams to the back. The outfit's front panels run straight down the shirt's front with its shoulders sitting on the shirt's shoulder seams, and its sleeves are printed along the shirt's sleeves to cuffs at the sleeve hems, showing a tweed jacket with chalk-dusted elbow patches. Turn the shirt around and the back carries the matching back of the outfit, printed edge to edge with nothing left plain. The outfit's fabric runs seamlessly over the shoulders and down the sleeves, every part of the shirt in the outfit's own colours and textures. The shirt is a standard T-shirt shape with a straight hem across the bottom. The printed top garment continues down the shirt to its straight hem, with at most a belt or sash at the waist. The print is cut exactly to the shirt, neck, shoulders, armholes, sleeves and hem are all covered in the outfit's own fabric. The uniform fills the whole straight-sided shirt shape edge to edge, the same width at chest, waist and hem. The shirt's sleeves are tailored to end at the elbow, exactly where the outfit's sleeves end. Everything is flat ink on opaque cotton, lace, tulle, fur, feathers, sequins, armour and metal appear as printed patterns. Only the outfit's fabric, trims and fastenings are pictured, spread across the entire shirt as a continuous pattern. It is the kind of novelty tee that tricks the eye from across a room. The tee is clearly a costume tee, not a plain shirt, it shows the lower garment's colours and pattern as a band across the hem, the headwear's emblem or crest worked into the chest and its pockets, flaps and trims, so anyone can tell at a glance what outfit it stands for. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed mid-tone brown tanned skin tone.

The outfit's front panels run straight down the shirt's front with its shoulders sitting on the shirt's shoulder seams, and its sleeves are printed along the shirt's sleeves to cuffs at the sleeve hems, showing a grey plush shark onesie. Front and back are both fully printed, the back showing how the same outfit looks from behind. The outfit's own cloth covers the whole shirt as one continuous print, so shoulders, sleeves and body are all in the outfit's colours. The shirt keeps the outline of an ordinary T-shirt, round neckline, straight side seams, sleeves, and a straight open hem. The printed top garment continues down the shirt to its straight hem, with at most a belt or sash at the waist. The print is cut exactly to the shirt, neck, shoulders, armholes, sleeves and hem are all covered in the outfit's own fabric. The outfit is laid out on the shirt's own rectangle shape, fully covering it from side seam to side seam. The shirt is a long-sleeved T-shirt matching the outfit's long sleeves, printed with the sleeves and cuffs all the way down to the wrist hems. The shirt is solid opaque cotton and every texture and sheen is a printed picture. Only the outfit's fabric, trims and fastenings are pictured, spread across the entire shirt as a continuous pattern. It is the kind of novelty tee that tricks the eye from across a room. The tee is clearly a costume tee, not a plain shirt, it shows the belt, straps and buckles of the outfit, the footwear's trim colours as stripes on the cuffs and hem and the outfit's badges, insignia and emblems, so anyone can tell at a glance what outfit it stands for. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed mid-tone brown tanned skin tone.

The printed outfit runs from the neckline to the hem and from one sleeve hem to the other, its shoulders on the shirt's shoulder seams, showing a hardened leather flight jacket with scale pads. The back of the shirt is printed just as completely, edge to edge, with the back of the same outfit, its back collar, shoulder blades and the backs of both sleeves. One continuous print of the outfit's cloth covers the shirt from collar band to hem and out to both sleeve hems. The shirt is a standard T-shirt shape with a straight hem across the bottom. Only the upper garment is printed, running all the way down to the shirt's straight hem. The outfit's cloth runs unbroken from the collar band across both shoulders and down both sleeves to their hems, so every part of the shirt is outfit cloth. The outfit is laid out on the shirt's own rectangle shape, fully covering it from side seam to side seam. The shirt is a long-sleeved T-shirt matching the outfit's long sleeves, printed with the sleeves and cuffs all the way down to the wrist hems. All textures, transparencies and sheens are printed patterns on solid cotton. The picture is only the garment, its cloth, seams, buttons and trims laid flat across the whole shirt like a sewing pattern. It also shows a printed collar around the real neckline. It is a trompe-l'oeil T-shirt, a plain cotton shirt pretending to be the outfit. It carries enough of the costume to be unmistakable, the lower garment's colours and pattern as a band across the hem, the footwear's trim colours as stripes on the cuffs and hem and the headwear's emblem or crest worked into the chest, all in the outfit's own colours. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed mid-tone brown tanned skin tone.

Turn the shirt around and the back carries the matching back of the outfit, printed edge to edge with nothing left plain. The outfit's cloth runs unbroken from the collar band across both shoulders and down both sleeves to their hems, so every part of the shirt is outfit cloth. The uniform fills the whole straight-sided shirt shape edge to edge, the same width at chest, waist and hem. A long-sleeved shirt is used so the outfit's long sleeves fit exactly, printed full length to the shirt's wrist hems. Everything is flat ink on opaque cotton, lace, tulle, fur, feathers, sequins, armour and metal appear as printed patterns. The picture is only the garment, its cloth, seams, buttons and trims laid flat across the whole shirt like a sewing pattern. It may also show a flat printed collarbone and upper chest of a flat printed mid-tone brown tanned skin tone showing at the open neckline, all as flat ink. It also shows printed cuffs where the sleeves end. It is a trompe-l'oeil T-shirt, a plain cotton shirt pretending to be the outfit. To read as a costume rather than a plain top, it adds the outfit's badges, insignia and emblems, the belt, straps and buckles of the outfit and the lower garment's colours and pattern as a band across the hem, bold and large enough to identify the outfit from across a room. The outfit's front panels run straight down the shirt's front with its shoulders sitting on the shirt's shoulder seams, and its sleeves are printed along the shirt's sleeves to cuffs at the sleeve hems, showing a black robe with white bands. Turn the shirt around and the back carries the matching back of the outfit, printed edge to edge with nothing left plain. One continuous print of the outfit's cloth covers the shirt from collar band to hem and out to both sleeve hems. It is an ordinary T-shirt in shape, with a straight open hem and sleeves cut to match the outfit's sleeves. Only the upper garment is printed, running all the way down to the shirt's straight hem. The outfit's collar meets the real collar band, its shoulders sit on the real shoulder seams and its sleeves fill the real sleeves, all in one piece of printed cloth. The outfit is laid out on the shirt's own rectangle shape, fully covering it from side seam to side seam. The shirt is a long-sleeved T-shirt matching the outfit's long sleeves, printed with the sleeves and cuffs all the way down to the wrist hems. The shirt is solid opaque cotton and every texture and sheen is a printed picture. The print is the garment itself, flat and unfolded over the shirt, in its own cloth and colours. It also shows a printed collar continuing the outfit up to the neckline and printed cuffs and wrists at the sleeve hems. It is the kind of novelty tee that tricks the eye from across a room. It carries enough of the costume to be unmistakable, the collar, neckwear and fastenings of the outfit, the footwear's trim colours as stripes on the cuffs and hem and the belt, straps and buckles of the outfit, all in the outfit's own colours. Any printed skin, such as hands, wrists, neck, chest or forearms, is in a flat printed mid-tone brown tanned skin tone.
